costGuide.labourLine: Fitting a UFDA typically takes 8-11 hours at ~£65/hr (independent specialist rates) - confirm exact labour costs when comparing your quotes .

failures.title: Ford UFDA Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Injector Failure and Leak-Off Issues - 2006-2013 models
items.whatHappens: The piezoelectric injectors in the UFDA are prone to seal degradation, leading to fuel leak-off and carbon buildup around the injector seats. This can cause rough idling, difficult cold starts, and in severe cases, fuel dilution in the engine oil, which degrades lubrication.
items.repairVsReplace: If caught early, replacing the injectors and seals (£300-£800) is sufficient. However, if fuel dilution has degraded the oil and caused bearing wear, a full reconditioned replacement is the only reliable, long-term solution.

items.title: DPF Clogging and Turbocharger Strain
items.whatHappens: The UFDA is highly sensitive to urban, stop-start driving, which prevents the Diesel Particulate Filter (DPF) from completing active regeneration cycles. A blocked DPF increases exhaust backpressure, which subsequently starves the turbocharger of proper airflow and can lead to premature turbo bearing failure.
items.repairVsReplace: A standalone DPF clean or replacement (£400-£1,200) may resolve the issue if the turbo remains healthy. If the turbo has already suffered oil starvation or bearing wear (£800-£2,000), a full engine replacement is often more cost-effective than repairing both components on a high-mileage unit.

failures.goodYearsLine: The UFDA is generally considered a robust and durable commercial-grade engine. Failures are overwhelmingly tied to poor maintenance (extended oil intervals) or unsuitable urban driving cycles, rather than inherent design flaws .

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the UFDA
variants.intro: The UFDA engine code is stamped on a machined pad on the engine block, typically located near the junction of the engine and the gearbox, or clearly marked on the cylinder head cover. It is also explicitly listed on your vehicle's V5C registration document under the engine capacity or code section.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement UFDA - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used UFDA is a viable option primarily for commercial van hosts (like the Transit) where the vehicle's residual value is low, provided the donor engine comes with a verifiable service history proving the injectors and DPF have been meticulously maintained. The risk of inheriting hidden turbo wear makes this a calculated gamble. Learn more about sourcing used engines.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: This is the most recommended route for the UFDA, especially for Mondeo owners. A proper reconditioning process will replace the injectors, seals, and often the turbocharger as standard, directly addressing the engine's most common failure points while retaining the sound, durable 2.2L block. Explore reconditioned engines.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full rebuild is justified if the original UFDA suffered catastrophic failure due to prolonged oil starvation or severe DPF-induced turbo failure. A quality rebuild will include new bearings, a machined block, and revised cooling components to prevent recurrence of the factory weaknesses. See options for rebuilt engines.

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: For complete peace of mind, our network offers nationwide supply and fit, ensuring the replacement is installed by Ford-trained specialists and backed by a minimum 12-month warranty.
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: The UFDA is typically found in Ford Mondeo Mk4 and Transit Mk7 models valued between £1,500 and £6,000 . With reconditioned replacement costs starting around £1,500, the investment is generally safe for well-maintained, higher-value examples. However, for early Mondeo Mk4 or high-mileage Transit examples valued under £2,500, the replacement cost may approach or exceed 60% of the vehicle's total market value, making a thorough pre-purchase evaluation essential.

items.question: How much does a Ford UFDA engine replacement cost?
items.answer: A reconditioned Ford UFDA engine costs between £1,500 and £2,800 for supply-only, with fully fitted prices typically ranging from £2,020 to £3,515. Supply-only used units start around £500 but carry higher latent DPF and turbo wear risks. Labour for a UFDA swap typically takes 8-11 hours at independent specialist rates. A proper reconditioned unit addresses the known injector and cooling weaknesses, offering better long-term value.

items.question: What is the most common Ford UFDA engine failure?
items.answer: The most documented Ford UFDA failures are piezoelectric injector seal degradation and DPF clogging, typically occurring between 80,000 and 150,000 miles. Symptoms include rough idling, difficult cold starts, and increased exhaust backpressure straining the turbocharger. If ignored, fuel dilution from leaking injectors can degrade the engine oil, leading to catastrophic bearing wear. Strict adherence to Ford's specified oil change intervals is the most effective preventative measure.

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned UFDA engine?
items.answer: A reconditioned Ford UFDA is strongly recommended over a used unit due to the engine's sensitivity to maintenance history. Used UFDA engines, especially from high-mileage Transit vans, often inherit latent turbocharger wear or DPF blockages that are not immediately visible. A quality reconditioning process replaces the injectors, seals, and often the turbocharger as standard, resetting the engine's reliability clock. The modest price premium for a reconditioned unit is quickly offset by the included 12-to-24-month warranty.
